stem: An ad-tech company's platform team needs one load balancer that routes HTTP requests to different target groups based on the URL path of each request.

choices.text: An Application Load Balancer, using path-based routing rules to send requests to the matching target group
A Network Load Balancer, since it offers the lowest possible latency for the traffic
A Gateway Load Balancer, placed in front of a third-party inspection appliance
Amazon Route 53 weighted routing records pointing at each target group's own endpoint

rationale: An Application Load Balancer operates at the application layer and supports path- and host-based routing, so it can inspect the URL path of an HTTP request and send it to the matching target group, which is exactly this requirement. A Network Load Balancer operates at the connection level and has no concept of an HTTP URL path to route on, even though it offers very low latency for raw TCP/UDP traffic. A Gateway Load Balancer exists to transparently pass traffic through third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls; it is not designed to route application requests by path. Route 53 weighted routing distributes DNS answers across endpoints by weight; it operates before a connection is even made and cannot inspect an HTTP request's URL path the way an ALB rule can.
